UNMET: [fix-code] RQFROM-4 | WHY: The issue states "without `--resume` the run refuses … even when the run would otherwise resume by itself (an automatic resume does not count). This is the behaviour on main, and it stays." The code narrows the flat-file guard to `status=interrupted` only: `if [[ "$_fsg_status" == "interrupted" ]]` (the guard at the comment "narrowed to interrupted-status only" around `_fsg_status == "interrupted"`). With `status=in_progress`, auto-resume fires, sets `resume_mode=true`, and the final post-auto-resume guard at `if [[ -n "$from_stage" ]] && ! $resume_mode` does not fire — so `--from-stage` without `--resume` on an `in_progress` run succeeds, contradicting R4a. The existing test in `pipeline-resume-test.sh` was changed from `status:"in_progress"` to `status:"complete"` with the explicit comment "Using in_progress would auto-resume instead, changing the expected error … #1805 moved the check after auto-resume so in_progress state auto-resumes and bypasses the check." This confirms the behavioral regression and the test change that conceals it. | QUOTE: core/pipeline/runner.sh | if [[ "$_fsg_status" == "interrupted" ]]; then

ANSWER lens-correctness-code finding 2 (opened by review_lenses): wrong — RQLOOP-1 and DSCMBR-1 state the documented interrupt scenario: build=complete, test=aborted in iter k; the test correctly covers exactly that scenario. The uncovered edge case the finding names — "test has status 'complete' from iter N-1 and build already completed in iter N" (the all-complete pre-scan path) — is not described in any stated requirement; a gap in that path would not make RQLOOP-1 or DSCMBR-1 fail. The finding identifies a coverage improvement beyond the issue's acceptance contract, not a missing requirement.
